subject: Store ui.R and server.R on the web

messages.author: 16edd76f6ee2b5b8
messages.subject: Store ui.R and server.R on the web
parts:
Hi,

I was wondering if it would be possible to store the ui.R and server.R on the web, and use runApp() with a web link, instead of the local address (e.g., like the address of the folder in which ui.R and server.R are stored). I wrote something that runs perfectly on my computer, but it didn't work when I stored them on the web and use the web link with runApp(). Did I do something wrong or does shiny not support it? The error message I got is: Error in setwd(appDir) : cannot change working directory, which makes sense since R probably can't set a web directory as its working directory. 

Thanks!

Best,
Xiao

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Store ui.R and server.R on the web
parts:
You're right that it can't set the remote URL as the working directory. Shiny currently doesn't support running applications from arbitrary URLs. But you can post applications on https://gist.github.com, and then use the runGist() function, which will download and run them.

-Winston

messages.author: d34d025a513c07fc
messages.subject: Re: Store ui.R and server.R on the web
parts:
If you are trying to run the application from a remote server, it won't work, because the server needs to know how to run the R part of the Shiny application.

If you sign up for the Shiny server beta program, you will be able to deploy Shiny apps on glimmer.rstudio.com, so that people will be able to use the app by simply visiting a webpage. See the "Over the web" section of this page:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#deployment

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: Store ui.R and server.R on the web
parts:
We've fixed the behavior of runGist. We're going to release a new version of Shiny (with this fix) to CRAN today or tomorrow, but if you want to use the fixed version right away, you can install it with devtools:

# If devtools isn't already installed, run
# install.packages('devtools')
library(devtools)
install_github('shiny', 'rstudio')


Once that's done, runGist() should work again.

-Winston
